description:
This letterpress print needed some rainbow ink and it goes out to all of those who love Dolly Parton. Since our last two Dolly quotes received very positive responses from our viewers, we thought we’d print another in our print shop at the Sacramento History Museum.

In this video, Channey letterpress printed a quote by Dolly. Set in 60 point Caslon font, the print states, “The way I see it, if you want the rainbow, you got to put up with the rain! -Dolly Parton.” This was printed with a gradient of red, yellow, blue, and purple ink using our Washington hand press, which was made in 1852. Sixty prints were made on this press run.

title: The Motor That Brings Faces Alive
description:
Kinetic sculptures bridge the gap between static art and robotics by relying on hidden internal mechanisms to create lifelike illusions. Inside this particular piece, a carefully concealed small motor serves as the beating mechanical heart of the artwork. As the motor engages, it drives an intricate network of specialized wire linkages and gears that are precisely calibrated to control the facial features.
The primary focus of this internal engineering is the manipulation of the sculpture's eyes. By translating the continuous rotational force of the motor into subtle, deliberate panning motions, the hidden wire mechanism allows the eyes to shift and scan the room slowly. This calculated movement completely transforms the viewer's experience. It breaks the cold, unsettling stillness typically associated with traditional portrait busts, instantly making the sculpted face appear eerily alive and intensely aware of its surroundings.
Merging fine art sculpting with basic animatronics requires masterful precision, where the illusion relies entirely on keeping the complex metal skeleton hidden beneath the smooth exterior. The result is a captivating piece of dynamic art that commands absolute attention in any gallery space simply by looking back at the audience.
